description:
Companion to bd:JMAP-ic0j.8, applied to contacts-server.

\`crate-jmap-contacts-server/src/memory.rs\` carries the exact same full-rescan pattern that JMAP-ic0j.8 just removed from calendars-server:

- Line 201: \`fn recompute_address_books_with_contents(&mut self, account_id: &str)\` — scans all ContactCard objects per mutation.
- Callers (full-rescan after every relevant mutation):
  - Line 274: seed_object
  - Line 755: create_object
  - Line 848: update_object
  - Line 878: destroy_object
  - Line 939: copy_object (the copy_email-analog for ContactCard)

Five call sites; same O(N) per mutation, O(N²) ingest cost as calendars-server had.

Fix: mirror JMAP-ic0j.8's reverse-index counter approach:
- Replace \`address_books_with_contents: HashSet<Id>\` with \`address_book_card_counts: HashMap<Id, u32>\`.
- Add \`apply_contact_card_index_delta(&mut self, account_id, old, new)\` that diffs the \`addressBookIds\` sets.
- For seed_object: keep full rescan (no old state).
- For create / update / destroy / copy: extract old + new from the function-local JSON and call the delta helper.

Per workspace AGENTS.md "Canonical Templates", the canonical jmap-mail-server doesn't have this pattern at all (different domain — no per-mailbox reverse index). Calendars and contacts share the structure because Calendar/Event and AddressBook/ContactCard have the same containment shape. Calendars-server now has the canonical fix for this contained-object-counter pattern in the extension-server family; contacts-server should follow.

Tasks-server's memory.rs line 139 references "the previous full-scan recompute was O(N)" — it already has the fix. Verify by inspection (not in scope here) that tasks-server's approach matches calendars-server's; if it doesn't, a third bead handles the alignment.

P3 — same efficiency concern as JMAP-ic0j.8, not present-day correctness. Filed promptly so the workspace doesn't drift further.
title: Mirror JMAP-ic0j.8 in contacts-server: recompute_address_books_with_contents is O(N) per mutation
